## Description

{gtsummary} is the most widely used R package for creating
presentation-ready summary tables across the R ecosystem. It provides an
elegant and flexible way to summarize data sets, regression models, and
more, with sensible defaults and a high degree of customization.

In this seminar, we will introduce {gtsummary} and walk through how it
fits into a reproducible reporting workflow. Topics include:

-   **{gtsummary} fundamentals:** Creating demographic and summary
    tables with `tbl_summary()`, adding statistics, p-values, and
    overall columns, and customizing labels and formatting.

-   **Combining and extending tables:** Hierarchical summaries,
    merging and stacking tables, and choosing a print engine to export
    to HTML, Word, PDF, and more.

-   **Analysis Results Data (ARD):** How {gtsummary} and ARDs work
    together by design, so the numbers in your tables are traceable and
    reusable.

By the end of the session, you will know how to get started with
{gtsummary} and where to go next to tailor it to your own work.

[**Daniel D. Sjoberg**](https://www.danieldsjoberg.com/){.instructor-name}

[Executive Director of Data Science & Clinical Data Analytics, Kardigan (he/him)]{.instructor-role}

Daniel leads the Data Science and Clinical Analytics groups at Kardigan. Previously was a Senior Principal Innovation Data Scientist and Real-time Analytics Group Lead at Genentech, a Lead Data Science Manager at the Prostate Cancer Clinical Trials Consortium, and an academic biostatistician at Memorial Sloan Kettering Cancer Center for 13 years. He enjoys R package development, creating many packages on [CRAN](https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/), [R-Universe](https://ddsjoberg.r-universe.dev/ui#packages), and [GitHub](https://github.com/ddsjoberg). He's a co-organizer of [rainbowR](https://rainbowr.netlify.app/) and of the [R Medicine Conference](https://rconsortium.github.io/RMedicine_website/), and a recipient of the Brian Bole Award for Excellence from Open Source in Pharma and the ASA Innovation in Programming Award.
